summary: This is a doc-only bookkeeping diff (PROGRESS.md + ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml), not the GP-20 code change itself -- the real implementation (wouldCreateCycle() DFS cycle detector in src/lib/loop-prevention.ts, recordTaskEscalationEdge() in the new src/lib/task-dependency-graph.ts, and the crm-service.ts wiring) already merged separately as PR #465 (commit 4cffe82d), which I pulled and read directly rather than trusting the self-report -- the DFS logic is correct (walks from toTaskId looking for a path back to fromTaskId before allowing the new edge) and matches the claim text. Verification against the live repo shows the ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml portion of the supplied diff is stale/already-landed: PR #467 (same branch, chore/gp-20-claim-completed) already merged that exact move-to-recently_completed edit into main (merge commit 33b615ba, confirmed via gh pr view showing state MERGED), so a direct two-dot `git diff origin/main HEAD` shows zero remaining difference for that file -- the only genuinely new, unmerged content is the PROGRESS.md update, which truthfully reflects verified reality (PR #465 and PR #467 merge commits both exist and match what PROGRESS.md claims). No .github/workflows/** files are touched. No security, schema, or auth-relevant paths are touched. Safe to merge autonomously.
issues: The diff supplied for review was a three-dot (git diff origin/main...HEAD) diff against a stale merge-base, so it displays the ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml move as pending change when it was in fact already merged to main via PR #467 before this review started -- the real outstanding diff is PROGRESS.md only. Not a blocker here since applying it is a no-op for that file, but future dispatches should generate review diffs with two-dot comparison against current origin/main to avoid showing already-merged content as pending.
